strategyResult.strategy: Given elevated geopolitical risk (Iran conflict, oil price volatility), the portfolio is shifted toward defensive income, broad diversification, and reduced single-stock concentration. High-cash positions are deployed into quality income ETFs and diversified equity ETFs, while zero-target legacy holdings are trimmed or eliminated to simplify. Account-type optimization ensures tax-efficient placement: high-growth US equity in TFSA, income/dividends in registered accounts, and Canadian-focus in non-registered for dividend tax credit eligibility.

strategyResult.notes: OVERALL PORTFOLIO ASSESSMENT: The portfolio spans C$666K across 5 accounts with strong structural bones but execution gaps — most accounts have significant drift from targets, particularly Registered-4 (PHYS at 3.4% vs 25% target) and Non-registered (54.7% cash). KEY GEOPOLITICAL RESPONSE: Iran war risk and oil volatility favor (1) PHYS gold in Registered-4 as primary hedge — build aggressively to 25%; (2) XME for commodity inflation exposure; (3) XDIV.TO for defensive Canadian dividend income; (4) SGOV/ZMMK.TO as short-term cash equivalents. TAX EFFICIENCY OPTIMIZATION: Canadian dividend stocks (NA.TO, XDIV.TO, MFC.TO, RY.TO) are best in non-registered for the dividend tax credit — currently MFC.TO and RY.TO are in Registered-1 which is suboptimal but cannot be transferred; eliminate them there and hold Canadian dividend exposure via XDIV.TO instead. US equities (NVDA, MSFT, ABBV, COST) are correctly sheltered in registered accounts. ETF CATEGORY WINNERS BY ACCOUNT: US Equity — XSP.TO (Registered-2, hedged), XEQT.TO (Registered-3/4, all-in-one); Canadian Dividend — XDIV.TO (all registered); Income/Covered Call — SPYI + QQQI (Registered-1); Bonds — ZAG.TO (Registered-4 + Non-reg); Gold — PHYS (Registered-4). VE (Europe ETF) is not recommended as XEU.TO and XEF.TO already cover international developed markets adequately. CIF (CI Financial) is not recommended due to financial sector concentration risk alongside existing bank holdings.
